title: Review of lab 1's active-droplets/ad3-membrane (IBD): the self-made amphiphile shell and division replicate on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (psi rim/core 3.74 and 3.55, membrane-like in 68/74 and 59/66 droplets; 14 and 10 persistent splits, generation 4 and 2, 0 merges); the shell is inert (s = 0)
summary: Labkit packs of threads/active-droplets/worlds/ad3-membrane/world.py, unchanged, 128^2, 200 frames. Fuel-fed Cahn-Hilliard droplets grow and divide without merging: seed 3, 14 splits all persistent, generation 4; seed 4, 14 splits, 10 persistent, generation 2; 16 droplets at the end on both. The amphiphile psi is made only by the droplets' fuel reaction (kp * prod, prod = k u c^2) and drifts up grad |grad phi|^2: rim/core 3.74 and 3.55, rim/out 10.8 and 11.3, membrane-like individually in 68 of 74 and 59 of 66 droplets. Reading world.py: the back-reaction s is 0 in P, so psi does not act on the droplets.

verdicts.limitation: As lab 1 said, the shell is inert (s = 0: no back-reaction), so it is a quasi-equilibrium coating of a droplet-made species that does no work; it counts for L3 under the quasi-equilibrium clause only, and a 1-2 px shell has no resolution test here. Division is the known ad1 fuel mechanism. No source-ablation rerun.
